newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise in wk ending 7/4.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise in wk ending 7/4.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages rose during the week ending July 4, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgages rose four basis points in the week to an average 7.62 percent from 7.58 percent.
Fifteen-year mortgages inched up to an average 7.15 percent from 7.13 percent.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages were nearly unchanged at 5.67 percent in the week, up from 5.66 last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.14 percent, the 15-year 7.67 percent and the ARM 5.94 percent.

"The economy is currently growing at a moderate pace as evidenced by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term rates at their current level and the employment figures released this morning," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said in a statement.

"This alleviates concerns of an overheated market and reduces pressure on interest rates. As a matter of fact, we may even see rates drop back to 7.5 percent in light of the unemployment figures," Nothaft added.

Lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, up slightly from last week. 15-year loans averaged 1.7 percent, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.45 percent on ARM loans, down from 1.5 in the previous week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
